Thank you for your submission.

This appears to mostly be a modified MIT license, with (1) a different second paragraph imposing a vaguely-worded copyleft-style obligation; and (2) an additional sentence at the end referring to your company. I _have not_ yet run a comparison to confirm whether there are any other changes.

In the section on "How license meets inclusion principles", your submission did not explain how this license satisfies the [SPDX Inclusion Principles](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/blob/main/DOCS/license-inclusion-principles.md).

In particular, looking at the "Other factors" on that page:

1. The sentence from your license which states "The above rights are granted on the condition that the Software remains open source and freely available to all users." -- it looks to me as though this is intended to be a copyleft-style obligation, but I'm not really sure how this would work in practice, since it isn't clear what is intended by having "the Software remain[] open source". Although vaguely worded, I could see ways that this might align with some of the open source-like definitions in Other Factor 1, but I can't really say for certain.

2. The added sentence at the end, together with the name of the license, suggests that this is intended for use primarily by your company, rather than by the broader community. While the email address could be accommodated by XML markup, this still feels like it's a one-off license for your company rather than something in broader use.

3. In particular on "Other factor" 3, I don't see any evidence at all of "actual, substantial use such that it is likely to be encountered" in the broader community. The only projects linked or referenced above appear to have very limited usage and are not in any way evidence of substantial use of this license. A few quick searches on Google and GitHub showed zero use other than these personal projects.

For what it's worth, I am **not** impressed or convinced by the above comments in this thread that were added a few minutes after this submission was made. Three comments from what clearly appear to be related GitHub accounts do not give me any confidence that this is a license that has actual, **substantial** use.

I am not in favor of adding this license to the SPDX License List at this time, absent evidence of substantial use in the broader community.

Dear Mr. Winslow,  

I hope this message finds you well.  

I am the owner of GoSecureDNS.org. While our license is inspired by the MIT license, our primary goal for seeking inclusion in the SPDX License List is to bring awareness to the work we do at GoSecureDNS.org. Our mission is to provide security, privacy, and anonymity to users free of cost.  

We operate as a web hosting company (though I cannot disclose the name), and we work across multiple fields. However, all of our income is dedicated to supporting the free services and humanitarian efforts we provide. Despite operating at a loss for the past 4–5 months, we remain committed to offering as much as we can for free.  

To protect privacy and ensure that anyone can approach us without fear, we do not keep any records of the cases we handle. This policy allows people to share their problems with us securely and anonymously. As a result, we can only recall two specific cases:  
1. A man reported a fraud case involving over $100,000 but could not go to the police or other authorities. We stepped in and helped him resolve the issue.  
2. A woman approached us after her private video was leaked. We helped her navigate the situation and provided her with support.  

In addition to these, we have also assisted in resolving cases involving deepfake content.  

These examples reflect just a small portion of the work we do to assist individuals in need. Alongside these efforts, we offer free services such as parking pages, free security APIs, and more.  

We had plans to introduce a new API for secure data encryption and storage, but unfortunately, our budget constraints have delayed this initiative.  

Due to our limited resources, we have even hosted our domain, GoSecureDNS.org, on a shared server to save costs. However, all other critical data and services are securely hosted on dedicated servers that are not exposed to the web.  

The main reason for creating this license and seeking its inclusion in the SPDX License List is to raise awareness about GoSecureDNS.org and to potentially attract donations or funding. This would help us continue our mission of helping people and providing free, secure services to the community.  

At the end of the day, our goal is to support those in need and to operate in the most ethical and transparent manner possible.  

We would sincerely appreciate your support in this effort.  

Thank you for your time and consideration.  

Best regards,  
[I cannot disclose the name]
Owner, GoSecureDNS.org

Hello @gosecuredns, thank you for your message.

Your services sound like they have positive goals, and I wish you the best in your efforts.

However, the purpose of adding licenses to the SPDX License List is not to advertise any organization's services, or to raise awareness / enable funding for submitters' organizations. I encourage you in your efforts going forward, but this is not relevant to the question of whether or not the license meets the [license inclusion principles](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/blob/main/DOCS/license-inclusion-principles.md).

As I mentioned in my earlier comment, I don't believe it does, in particular the absence of substantial use of the license. And given your response about the primary purpose of adding this license being to promote your own service offerings, I am going to go ahead and close this submission as not accepted.
